text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures tumbled in late trade, but outperformed their U.S. counterparts after Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan said in his Congressional testimony he could not rule out a pre-emptive tightening of interest rates. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 103.01, down 0.36 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts tumbled as Greenspan said he saw inflationary risks in the U.S. economy and could not rule out a pre-emptive rate rise. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 112-19/32, down 16/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.
FRANCE - Bond futures lost ground on the Greenspan comments. The March bond future on the MATIF (exchange) in Paris settled at 132.00, down 0.22 from Tuesday's settlement price.
ITALY - Debt markets slipped lower in late trade after Greenspan's testimony. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 130.15, down 0.39 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices tumbled after Greenspan's much anticipated Congressional testimony. NEW YORK (Reuter) - Stocks and bonds tumbled Wednesday after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan voiced concern about soaring stock prices and said the central bank was ready to raise interest rates to ward off inflation.
The dollar jumped after Greenspan's remarks, since higher rates would make the currency more attractive to overseas investors.
Just after 12:20 p.m. in New York, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 66.96 points at 6,971.25 following a brief plunge of more than 101 points.

The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell almost 1-1/4 points, or $12.50 on a $1,000 bond, pushing its yield up to 6.75 percent from 6.66 percent on Tuesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

JAPAN - Key March 10-year Japanese government bond futures (JGBs) closed higher on dealers' short-covering, following a better-than-expected showing for the newly auctioned 10-year JGBs. In after-hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.20, unchanged from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Small transactions in dollars, marks and sterling provided much of the day's Eurobond activity. Dresdner launched a 500 million mark 10-year bond, LW Rentenbank a 300 million mark issue. Structured deals also surfaced. In dollars, Spintab set a $300 million FRN. OKB and FEK issued small sterling bonds. The World Bank said it would launch a euro Eurobond as soon as it became cost-effective to do so.
